# Does ros2_control already have a formal mechanism for different read/write rates for hardware components?

> **Current answer:** Yes. PR #1570 adds rw_rate to each ros2_control hardware component and updates the official documentation, parsing/scheduling implementation, and testing. The documentation example shows system, actuator, and sensor running at 500/200/250 Hz respectively; if not set, it follows controller_manager, and if higher, it only runs at controller_manager rate.

## Key terms

- Hardware component (硬件组件)
- Read/write rate (rw_rate) (读写频率)
- Controller manager (控制器管理器)
- Asynchronous hardware (异步硬件)

## Problem and symptoms

- How to configure different read/write rates for multiple hardware components?
- How to avoid reading low-frequency signals when position is 100 Hz and voltage is 0.1/1 Hz within a single hardware component?
- Fixed high-frequency read/write will cause low-frequency states to consume bandwidth, leading to retries, packet loss, and extra delay.

## Environment

- ros2_control rolling/master period; PR #1570 has been merged; specific ROS 2 release version needs to be checked for backport.

## Priority diagnostics

- First determine if different frequency signals can be assigned to different ros2_control hardware components.
- Distinguish between controller update rate, hardware component rw_rate, and the actual sampling rate of each state within a component.
- Expose timestamp or staleness of states used for reusing old values to prevent controllers from treating cached values as new samples.

## Attempts

- PR #1570 adds rw_rate to each hardware component.
- Maintainer suggests using counter/internal filtering to skip low-frequency voltage readings within a component, or splitting components.

## Effective fixes

- Across components: set rw_rate in ros2_control tag; actual rate is limited by controller_manager rate when higher.
- Same component: update target state with counter/filter rules for low-frequency readings, skip periodic retention of previous values; or restructure into separate components.

## Result

- Component-level rw_rate has been merged and documented/tested; fine-grained interface for sub-state of state being updated by controller is not yet implemented in this thread.

## Limitations

- PR #1570 corresponds to the parameter name and semantics of the merge version; different ROS 2 release versions need verification.
- The counter scheme for the same component is a maintainer's suggestion; no thread has been published with deployment testing.

## Safety notes

- When reusing old values, carry timestamp/validity and set timeout; expired temperature, voltage, or fault states should not be silently used for safety decisions.
